text:
support: Customer (NimbleHealth) flagged a billing charge for a request that aborted mid-stream. They say SDK closed the socket and the request was counted as a 5xx. request_id=rid_01FHX2ZK14

alex: Do we have the gateway logs for rid_01FHX2ZK14? customer provided sample trace + approximate time window (2024-12-05T14:23:10Z). They say client saw a tcp FIN immediately after first chunk.

kate-cs: Customer impact: charged for ~140 tokens, saw 429 then a 5xx in our dashboard, unhappy. Wants charge review if it was client-initiated.

maria: grabbing logs now. quick note: we recently rolled out the proxy keepalive patch last week — possible race in half-close handling.

jordan: pasted gateway logs (excerpt):
```
[2024-12-05T14:23:10.123Z] rid=rid_01FHX2ZK14 client_conn=10.2.3.5 state=streaming received_chunks=1 bytes_sent=512 upstream_status=200
[2024-12-05T14:23:10.129Z] rid=rid_01FHX2ZK14 tcp_event=FIN from_client
[2024-12-05T14:23:10.130Z] rid=rid_01FHX2ZK14 gateway_metric=upstream_partial_close -> classified=5xx
```

alex: That classification is the bug. Our heuristic currently flags any mid-stream tcp FIN within 1s of stream start as gateway failure if upstream still sending. But if client sent FIN after receiving first chunk that's client-abort, not a server 5xx.

eng-runtime: Confirmed. The rule was intended to catch sudden network drops where server never sent tokens. Edge case: SDKs that do a client half-close to signal end-of-input close the write side but still read. Some proxies treat that as connection termination. We mis-translate that into a 5xx.

support: Customer supplied repro steps. Minimal curl reproducer (they used our JS SDK but curl reproduces):
```
# client sends request, then immediately half-closes (simulate via tcpkill or using socat)
curl -N -H 'Authorization: Bearer $KEY' -H 'Transfer-Encoding: chunked' \
  -d $'4\r\nping\r\n0\r\n\r\n' https://api.redwood.example/v1/stream?model=gpt-rl
# then client closes socket after first chunk (OS-level FIN)
```

maria: I ran the same locally against staging and reproduced classification. We'll need to change classification to check whether upstream already sent >0 non-empty chunks and response headers indicated 2xx before marking 5xx. If upstream_status=200 and bytes_sent>0 -> classify as client_abort and bill accordingly.

jordan: Also saw a correlating spike in incorrect 5xx metrics between 14:20-14:35 after proxy update. @sre-bot deploying rollback patch to test.

sre-bot: Deploy started: rollback/keepalive-fix at 2024-12-06T03:12:00Z. CI tests: streaming-integration, chunked-heartbeat.

eng-runtime: Proposed fix (short):
1) when tcp FIN from client is observed, check gateway state: if response headers sent and token_count > 0 -> set outcome=client_disconnect.
2) add metric: misclassified_5xx_to_client_abort with tags {model, region}.
3) patch billing pipeline to exclude misclassified cases from automatic refunds until we finish manual review.

alex: For this customer, we should do an immediate manual refund for rid_01FHX2ZK14 and add a small credit for trouble. Kate, can you initiate?

kate-cs: On it. Filing refund request now and pinging customer with explanation + repro guidance (advise update to latest SDK which avoids premature half-close).

kate-cs: Message to customer drafted: "We reproduced the issue; our gateway misclassified your client-initiated stream close as a server error. We issued a refund for the charge and a credit for the inconvenience. We're rolling a fix to prevent future misclassification. Sorry for the friction." :pray:

eng-runtime: Will open a PR with the classification change and add unit tests for chunked flow + client FIN semantics. Assigning to @maria.

maria: PR opened: https://git.redwood.dev/eng/runtime/pulls/482 — includes testcases and metric. Requesting review from @alex and @jordan.

jordan: After rollback + fix, we'll backfill metrics and run a query to find other requests in that window that match pattern (bytes_sent > 0 + client FIN within 2s). I'll produce a list for billing to review.

support: Outcome: refund for nimblehealth issued, fix queued and deployed, metric added, and customer notified. Closing thread once post-deploy verification done.
